heading: Joint flexible fuel/hybrid vehicle commercialization initiative

children.heading: Eligible entity
children.text: The term “eligible entity” means—
a for-profit corporation;
a nonprofit corporation; or
an institution of higher education.

children.heading: Program
children.text: The term “program” means a program established under subsection (b).

tree.heading: Establishment
tree.text: The Secretary shall establish a program to improve technologies for the commercialization of—

children.text: a combination hybrid/flexible fuel vehicle; or
a plug-in hybrid/flexible fuel vehicle.

tree.heading: Grants
tree.text: In carrying out the program, the Secretary shall provide grants that give preference to proposals that—

children.text: achieve the greatest reduction in miles per gallon of petroleum fuel consumption;
achieve not less than 250 miles per gallon of petroleum fuel consumption; and
have the greatest potential of commercialization to the general public within 5 years.

tree.heading: Verification
tree.text: Not later than 90 days after August 8, 2005, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register procedures to verify—

children.text: the hybrid/flexible fuel vehicle technologies to be demonstrated; and
that grants are administered in accordance with this section.

tree.heading: Report
tree.text: Not later than 260 days after August 8, 2005, and annually thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report that—

children.text: identifies the grant recipients;
describes the technologies to be funded under the program;
assesses the feasibility of the technologies described in paragraph (2) in meeting the goals described in subsection (c);
identifies applications submitted for the program that were not funded; and
makes recommendations for Federal legislation to achieve commercialization of the technology demonstrated.

tree.heading: Authorization of appropriations
tree.text: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section, to remain available until expended—

children.text: $3,000,000 for fiscal year 2006;
$7,000,000 for fiscal year 2007;
$10,000,000 for fiscal year 2008; and
$20,000,000 for fiscal year 2009.
